niche_preference_profile: Prefers interfaces that feel immediately understandable and usable: strong visual hierarchy, clearly labeled sections and actions, readable layouts, and components that look complete rather than placeholder-like. They often favor light, calm, low-clutter screens with restrained styling for functional or trust-sensitive tasks, but they also respond positively to polished premium treatments when hierarchy and clarity are strong. They like concise, relevant information presented in scannable cards or rows, explicit status/context cues, and obvious primary actions. They dislike vague, hidden, overly decorative, crowded, or weakly structured layouts.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers screens with clear headline emphasis, strong grouping, obvious separation between primary and secondary information, and layouts that guide attention quickly.
Prefers explicit section headers, text-labeled actions, informative tabs or subtitles, and concrete naming that makes screen purpose and available actions obvious.
Prefers interfaces with easy-to-read text, strong contrast for content, and presentation styles that support fast scanning and comprehension.
Prefers simplified layouts with fewer decorative elements, fewer competing controls, muted or restrained backgrounds, and content kept in focus.
Prefers obvious primary actions, visible secondary options, and interaction patterns that make the next step or choice explicit.
Prefers content organized into distinct cards, rows, panels, or contained modules rather than flat or weakly defined surfaces.
Prefers useful supporting details such as status labels, counts, timestamps, source/freshness cues, and concise metadata when they improve understanding of the content.
